To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a watershed‐based segmentation of diatom cells is feasible, (ii) a hybrid approach is needed to avoid over‐ segmentation, and (iii) connected operators are an appropriate choice for the computation and the selection of markers.

a) the watershed segmentation is a powerful method for automatic segmentation of images of diatoms; b) the watershed method is sensitive to the choice of marker; c) connected operators are an efficient way to compute and select markers; d) the watershed method with connected operators is the best method for the segmentation of diatom image contours; e) the quality of the segmentation is crucial to the success of the classification; f) the segmentation is a key step for automatic identification of images of diatom cells

• We present a general framework for automatic contour extraction in diatom images, which is based on the hybrid watershed segmentation technique from mathematical morphology, with a new marker computation and selection method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a general framework for automatic image segmentation that is robust and efficient, and can be used to extract contours from images of any object.
the automatic identification of diatom species by computerized image processing and analysis.
the development of automatic image analysis techniques for the classification and identification of diatoms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the watershed segmentation method with the use of connected markers, as described in this paper, is the method of choice for the segmentation of diatom cells in the context of automatic identification.
the use of connected watershed segmentation for diatom contour extraction has been shown to be a promising approach for automatic identification of these objects.
the use of connected morphological operators for marker selection in watershed segmentation is a promising approach to automatic diatom image segmentation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a general framework for automatic contour extraction from diatom images.
the watershed segmentation method is the best choice for automatic segmentation of digital images of diatoms.
we have developed and tested a new method for the extraction of diatom images that can be used in automatic classification systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the watershed segmentation is an appropriate tool to segment diatom images.
a watershed‐based segmentation method can be used for automatic segmentation of complex diatom images.
the watershed segmentation method is well adapted to the problem of segmentation of diatom cells.
